note: Re-judged 2026-11-20 by an independent agent after 1b0198fb0d changed the negative TestMobikeAuthWithoutNATTSocketKeepsBaseIKE. RFC 4555 Section 3.3: "implementations that support both this specification and NAT Traversal MUST change to port 4500 if the correspondent also supports both, even if no NAT was detected between them". The negative gained an assertion that neither the initiator nor the responder SA sits on port 4500 without NAT-T support, beside the unchanged check that no IKE_AUTH carries MOBIKE_SUPPORTED: that is the case just outside the clause, where the correct answer is no float. The positive TestMobikeAuthNegotiation is byte-identical: through mbAuthHandshake it binds NAT-T sockets only, sends to the port-500 stand-in, fails on NATDetected and requires the IKE_AUTH on the NAT-T socket with the non-ESP marker, so a missing float delivers nothing and goes red. Verdict stands.
